visualStyle.lighting: harsh Texas daylight, dim motel interiors

analysis.themes: A welder takes cartel money and is hunted by something closer to fate than a man — Sheriff Bell narrates his own obsolescence against a violence he can't comprehend.
analysis.atmosphere: Relentless, scoreless tension; the Texas desert offers no comfort and the film offers less.
analysis.narrative: A chase thriller that refuses its own climax — the decisive events happen offscreen, because the film's subject is resignation, not rescue.
analysis.visual: Deakins' landscapes make men small; the Coens' framings turn motel rooms into killing geometry.
analysis.characters: Chigurh is an ideology wearing a man; Bell is decency outlived; Moss is the fool who thought he could outrun consequence.
